posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
thegayjewishguy2023 said:
I guess the part that confuses me the most is the difference between control switches and self-switches as well as variables.
Click to expand...
Self-switches only affect the current event.
Switches can be accessed anywhere in the game.
Both of these are boolean operators meaning they can only exist as a yes or no (true or false/ 1 or 0)
Variables can also be accessed by any event anywhere. Think of these as number containers or information containers.
The current problem Turan seems to be referencing is that, according to him (I haven't kept up with the post history), you keep making the same mistake which is having a blank event page.
The game references event pages right to left.
So the right most event page has the highest priority.
However on the left side of the event window you have various conditions you can enable. When those conditions are met, that event page will activate.
However page priority still takes precedent. Only 1 event page can be active at a time. So the current active page will be:
The right most page that has the most conditions being met.
What this means is that if you have 2 event pages with the exact same conditions "If switch 1 is on" then the right most page will take priority.
In your case, the problem you faced in this post was that neither event page had any conditions. So, the event will run:
The right most event page with 0 conditions.
Your right most page (page 2) had nothing on it. Therefore when you ran the event, nothing happened.
Using self-switches prevents you from having to create a specific event switch for every single event. Instead, if you want an event to only happen once, you can just use that event's set of self switches.
The "event start" (such as you dialogue) is 0 self switches (all self-switches are set to off - their default state).
When the event is over, you turn on self switch A.
Create a new event page.
Now here's the part I think you messed up on.
On the left panel of the event page, make sure to check the "self switch" box to tell the event "When THIS self switch is ON, use THIS event page"
Good luck with you game, I hope that broke down the problem for you!

Please follow the link to the starting point tutorial in my signature and work through it.
It contains links to other tutorials, especially to tutorials that are in the form of games themselves.
especially the variables guide game and one of the eventing tutorials games might help you.
It is extremely difficult to learn the maker on your own, you need a tutorial to follow through to learn at least the basics - and that usually takes most people a month or so with a scrap project.
And watching a video tutorial is usually wasted time (imho) because video tutorials don't give you the time to experiment on your own and are usually too short to contain everything you need to know.
